title: This Lizard Shrinks Up to 20 Percent of Its Length to Survive Famine

scenes.text: A lizard shrinks its own body to survive.
Marine iguanas on the Galapagos eat algae from the sea.
In El Nino years, the algae thins out and food runs short.
Researchers watched about six thousand iguanas through four El Nino events.
They got up to twenty percent shorter during famine.
Then they grew back when food returned.
A lizard that shrinks to survive. Now watch it again.

description:
A lizard shrinks its own body to survive.
Marine iguanas on the Galapagos can lose up to twenty percent of their length during El Nino famines, then grow back when food returns.
Would you shrink to survive?
first_comment: Bonus: scientists still debate exactly how it happens. Do the bones really shorten?
